outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms -- including risk for wind damage, large hail and a few tornadoes -- are expected from parts of the Ohio Valley southwestward into the mid and lower Mississippi Valley and Tennessee Valleys, and into the southern Plains. An enhanced threat for wind damage may occur across parts of the lower Ohio/mid Mississippi/Tennessee Valleys.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: An energetic short-wave upper trough -- phased with a weaker system crossing northern Mexico at the start of the period -- will sweep across the Plains and into the Great Lakes and Midwest/Ohio Valley today and tonight. Flanking the progressing trough, ridging will persist over both the western and eastern portions of the country. At the surface, a low is forecast to deepen with time while shifting northeast out of the Kansas/Oklahoma vicinity across Missouri and into the Midwest through the day. In conjunction, a sharpening cold front will sweep southeast across the central U.S. a the leading edge of a surge of cold Canadian air. By early evening, the front should extend from the low -- over the northern Indiana vicinity -- southwest across the lower Ohio and mid Mississippi Valleys and into east Texas, with a band of showers and thunderstorms in the vicinity of the advancing boundary. By the end of the period, the front will likely be cresting the Appalachians, while convection will likely have weakened to below severe levels. ...Lower Great Lakes southwest to parts of eastern Texas and the lower Mississippi Valley... sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, a broadly cyclonic pattern will be restored over much of the central U.S. this period, mainly because of height falls related to a strong shortwave trough now apparent in moisture-channel imagery over the northern/central High Plains. This perturbation should strengthen gradually as it moves roughly eastward through the period. By 00Z, the trough should extend from parts of MN/IA southwestward over KS. By 12Z, it should reach Lower MI, northern IN, southern IL and the Mid-South. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a frontal-wave low over eastern KS, with cold front southwestward across northwestern OK and the TX Panhandle. A warm front was drawn from the low eastward over central MO, southern IL, central IN, and east-central KY. The warm front, reinforced baroclinically by extensive convective precip now to its north over portions of IL/IN/OH, should move northeastward across southern/central parts of IL/IN/OH through the day, perhaps reaching northern IN and west-central/northwestern OH. sections.title: Ohio Valley to TX coastal plain
sections.text: Scattered to locally numerous thunderstorms, mainly in broken to solid bands, are expected to develop along and ahead of the surface cold front beginning around midday and lasting into tonight. As this convection crosses the outlook area, all modes of severe will be possible from a blend of QLCS features (LEWPs/bows), embedded supercells, and perhaps a few discrete to semi-discrete supercells ahead of the main line. The main threat in a coverage/duration sense still is damaging wind, especially over the enhanced-risk area. Within that, however, an enhanced afternoon/evening tornado risk also is becoming apparent from the region of the progressive warm frontal zone into IN/OH, southwestward to the MO Bootheel area. Tornado risk appears most concentrated in a northeastward-aligned corridor where at least a brief window is apparent for discrete or line-embedded supercells to encounter a favorable CAPE-shear parameter space. This includes: 1. A higher-buoyancy, strong deep-shear regime around the MO Bootheel and western KY, as well as 2. outlooks.summary: A Moderate Risk for thunderstorms producing widespread damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes exists over parts of the Ohio Valley and Mid-South regions.

sections.title: AR/MS northeastward through much of the OH/TN Valleys
sections.text: An active severe weather day is expected across the MS/OH/TN Valleys today with numerous strong/severe thunderstorms affecting a large area. The primary focus for severe storms will be a progressive and deepening shortwave trough moving across the central Plains. A deepening surface low and cold front in advance of this system will sweep across the risk area this afternoon through tonight, resulting in a fast-moving squall line extending from IL/IN/OH southward into the Mid South. Visible satellite imagery shows broken cloud cover across most of the warm sector, promoting heating and destabilization. Forecast soundings suggest a corridor of moderate CAPE values ahead of the front by mid-afternoon as thunderstorms begin to form. Initial activity may be supercellular in nature, with a risk of tornadoes (some strong) and large hail from northeast AR/western MS into parts of southern IL/IN and western KY. Eventually, the storms should congeal into a line with multiple bowing segments as it progresses across the MDT and ENH risk areas with the potential for widespread damaging winds and a few QLCS tornadoes.

sections.title: TX/LA
sections.text: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms have developed this morning over central TX, ahead of a southern stream shortwave trough. This activity will persist through the day and spread into LA, with a risk of large hail and damaging wind gusts. By mid-afternoon, thunderstorms are expected to form along the advancing cold front and affect these same areas.

sections.title: IN/OH
sections.text: A persistent cluster of thunderstorms is affecting much of central/northern IN and OH. The air mass south of the activity continues to warm, leading to a favorable environment for severe/supercell thunderstorms. This corridor remains in the higher tornado/damaging wind probability area for both warm frontal activity this afternoon, and the squall line activity later today. ..Hart.. 04/03/2018

sections.title: Mid-South into the OH/TN Valleys
sections.text: A pair of tornado watches (#26 and #27) currently extend from the OH Valley into the Mid-South. Airmass ahead of the southeastward advancing cold front continues to destabilize amidst modest moisture advection and diurnal heating. 18Z sounding from LZK showed little convective inhibition remaining, which is also evidenced by the recent uptick in storms along the front. This general trend is expected to continue. As storm coverage increases, the strongly sheared environment (i.e. 50 kt of 0-6 km bulk shear) favors storm organization and the general expectation is for numerous severe storms to develop along and just ahead of the front during the next several hours. Given the steep lapse rates across the region, large hail (some greater than 2" in diameter) will likely be the predominant threat for the next several hours. The surface winds are mostly veered but the strength of the winds and still favorable low-level curvature (0-1 km SRH from 200 to 300 m2 per s2 based on area VADs and recent mesoanalysis) will also support a tornado threat. An eventual transition to more of a linear storm mode will result in an increasing damaging wind threat. This overall scenario was depicted well

sections.title: Central/Northeast/Southeast TX and LA
sections.text: Thunderstorm activity which initiated during the late morning (and prompted the issuance of Severe Thunderstorm Watch #25) has become increasingly outflow dominant and lost intensity over the last two hours. As a result, the severe threat with these storms has also diminished. Additional thunderstorm activity has developed along the cold front, with that general trend expected to continue. Damaging wind gust and hail are the primary threats with these storms. Only change to outlook in this area is to update the western extent of the outlook based on current trends. Additional information for this area is available in the mesoscale discussion 207. ..Mosier.. 04/03/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1239 PM CDT Tue Apr 03 2018/

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms will remain capable of producing widespread damaging winds, hail, and a couple of tornadoes over parts of the Ohio Valley and Mid-South regions this evening and into the overnight hours.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Thunderstorms continue to gradually grow upscale/become more linearly organized with time, as expected due to the sharpening/advance of a strong cold front -- which now extends from Indiana southwest across the Mississippi Valley near the Arkansas/Tennessee border, and then continuing southwestward into east Texas. Evening RAOBs reveal steep lapse rates above a roughly 700 mb warm nose, and inverted V-type profiles below. With the relatively dry/warm boundary layer, the onset of diurnal cooling will allow the warm nose aloft to more substantially inhibit intense updrafts. This should result in a gradual decrease in convective intensity later this evening and into the overnight hours, particularly from the Mid South region, southward. Meanwhile farther north into the Ohio Valley region, stronger large-scale ascent has yielded weaker capping, but weaker instability is also noted due to an overall cooler boundary layer than areas farther south. Additional cooling/reduction in mixed-layer CAPE this evening and overnight suggests that storms will gradually diminish in intensity across this region as well. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms will increase in coverage across central/eastern Texas by mid afternoon. Large hail (some over two inches in diameter) and damaging winds will be the main threat. A tornado or two could develop as well, primarily across eastern Texas. Watch issuance is likely, but timing of issuance may range from late morning to mid afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite and radar data show initial mid-level convective development across parts of the northern Texas Hill Country. This evolution is likely aided by ascent ahead of a very apparent shortwave trough lifting northeast across Mexico currently. 12Z DRT/FWD observed soundings sampled an impressive elevated mixed layer, characterized by 700-500mb lapse rates around 9 C/km. Nonetheless, while this thermal profile is offering the potential for vigorous updraft accelerations, resultant convective inhibition offers considerable uncertainty with regards to timing of persistent deep convection. Considering the presence of this ample elevated buoyancy (MUCAPE upwards of 2500-3000 J/kg) and favorable effective shear for updraft organization, any persistent updrafts will likely possess a threat for very large hail. Additionally, despite their initially elevated nature, downdraft momentum will likely be strong enough to produce pockets of damaging winds. Moreover, through the afternoon, cells are expected to become rooted closer to the surface, and a threat for a tornado or two may materialize across east Texas. Despite the aforementioned conditional/uncertain nature of deep convective development, greater coverage is expected with the approach of the cold front and dryline. Therefore, watch issuance is likely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms are expected to increase in intensity this afternoon with a few tornadoes possible along with large hail. Additional severe storms are likely later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered storms persist from southern IL across central IN and into OH along and north of a warm front. This boundary will gradually shift northward due to boundary layer heating/mixing to the south and strengthening warm air advection via a backing 50-60 kt low-level jet. While some of the activity is currently elevated, a transition may occur in a few hours allowing storms along the warm front to become supercells and/or bows. Additional storms may also form south of the warm front as the air mass continues to destabilize, most likely across southern IN, far northern KY, and southwest OH. Wind profiles will become increasingly favorable for supercells and tornadoes throughout the day as the low deepens.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected to develop by mid afternoon across parts of Arkansas and Missouri, before spreading eastward through this evening. Damaging winds, tornadoes, and large hail will all be possible. Tornado watch issuance is expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Ahead of a cold front accelerating east/southeast, visible satellite depicts a zone of clearing/heating stretching from southeast Oklahoma to southern/central Illinois (in the wake of a pre-frontal bore). The 18Z LZK sounding suggests continued heating and northward boundary-layer moisture advection, combined with cooling aloft ahead of a Plains shortwave trough, should result in a corridor of minimal convective inhibition from western Arkansas to southern Illinois this afternoon. In turn, convection should gradually deepen within one or more bands of low-level confluence near/ahead of the front. Relatively uni-directional southwesterly flow will likely favor evolution towards small bands/bowing structures, with damaging winds as the chief threat. However, plentiful low-level shear (e.g., around 30-35 kt of 0-1km shear on the KPAH VWP) will likely encourage a few stronger low-level mesocyclones in embedded supercellular elements. With a destabilizing/moistening boundary layer established, these cells will be capable of a few tornadoes, a couple of which could be strong. Additionally, steep mid-level lapse rates and strong effective shear suggest any discrete development will be capable of large hail. Through evening, cells will likely grow upscale into one or more eastward-accelerating QLCSs capable of swaths of wind damage and a few embedded tornadoes. Tornado watch issuance is expected relatively soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Potential for isolated large hail and damaging winds remains from parts of the Texas Hill Country to the Arklatex.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small convective system has organized over central/eastern Texas this afternoon, characterized by maturing/trailing stratiform precipitation. More robust convection is situated along both the downshear and upshear flanks of this system. Along the downshear flank (Freestone/Anderson Counties), forward/eastward propagation may yield damaging wind gusts and isolated large hail reports through this evening. Meanwhile, upshear development over the northern Texas Hill Country may continue, and these cells would likely favor large hail as the primary threat. Farther north, cells are organizing along the cold front from DFW northeastward into southeast Oklahoma. These cells will push southeast through the evening, with locally damaging winds and isolated large hail possible. ..Picca.. 04/03/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storm extending from the Ohio River into central Ohio will pose a tornado, damaging wind and hail threat for the next several hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have increased in intensity over the past hour as destabilization continues via upstream heating and behind the lifting warm front. While initially disorganized, several robust storms have consolidated within the larger band of storms, with stronger indications of outflow as well as transient rotation. Surface analysis shows the warm front near Wilmington OH, where storms are currently crossing northeastward. Satellite imagery shows clearing into central OH as well, suggesting the front will continue into that area. While some storms may continue well into the cooler/more stable air mass, other cells will pose a threat as they develop over southeast IN into central KY and also cross the warm front. A few tornadoes remain possible with any supercells. Damaging wind and hail appears most likely away from the warm front in the near term as temperature/dewpoint spreads are higher, but all areas will experience another round of severe storms later this evening with the main cold front including a QLCS tornado and damaging wind threat. ..Jewell.. 04/03/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for large hail, tornadoes, and damaging winds persists across Tornado Watch 27.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A broken line of splitting/embedded supercells and small linear segments is advancing east across western portions of the ongoing tornado watch. Currently, large hail appears to be the primary threat, associated with more discrete cells. Several of these are exhibiting cyclonic rotation and more eastward propagation, enhancing streamwise vorticity near the surface. Assuming these cells can remain ahead of the accelerating cold front, the tornado threat should maximize later this evening as they approach the Mid-South and lower Ohio Valley. In time, convective mode will likely transition to more bowing/QLCS segments, with the primary threats evolving to damaging winds and embedded tornadoes across the Tennessee and Ohio Valleys. ..Picca.. 04/03/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe thunderstorm watch will be issued soon downstream of WW 25. Damaging wind and large hail will be the main concern into the evening hours across northeast LA, far southeast AR and into parts of western MS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A severe thunderstorm watch will be issued soon downstream of WW 25 across northeast LA, far southeast AR into parts of western MS. Dewpoints in the low to mid 60s to roughly the vicinity of the MS River are maintaining adequate instability to support continued severe threat. Furthermore, steep midlevel lapse rates and 0-6km shear greater than 40kt will support rotating storms capable of large hail. Additionally, fast storm motion and moderately steep low level lapse rates will support damaging wind gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A new downstream severe thunderstorm watch also will be needed across parts of central into southeast TX and far southwest LA. Large hail and damaging winds will be the main threat into the evening hours across this region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe thunderstorm watch 25 is set to expire at 23z. Storms were ongoing across eastern portions of the watch in east TX into northern LA. The surface cold front lags behind this convection from near OSA to LXY to just north of BMQ and then back to the west toward the Permian Basin. Initial, prefrontal convection has moved across parts of east TX, modifying the boundary layer. This likely will result less of a severe threat with convection now developing further northwest along the front as little time remains for adequate airmass recovery. Further south and west the airmass remains unmodified with dewpoints from the upper 60s to low 70s and moderate to strong instability from parts of central TX into far southwest LA. Further south of WW 25, a new watch will likely be needed as convection continues to develop along the southward surging cold front. At some point, the cold front will overtake the outflow boundary laid out by prior convection. This should align well with more favorable thermodynamic and kinematic environment and robust thunderstorm development is expected from the San Antonio to Houston to Lake Charles vicinity. Very steep midlevel lapse rates and adequate deep layer shear should maintain a large hail threat with some strong wind threat front any surging line segments.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will overspread the upper Ohio Valley region through 8-10 PM EDT, accompanied by some risk for hail, potentially damaging wind gusts and perhaps an isolated tornado.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A large cluster of thunderstorms appears to be maintained by lift associated with lower/mid tropospheric warm advection beneath strongest upper difluence, downstream of a vigorous short wave trough turning eastward into the upper Mississippi Valley. Activity is expected to persist into this evening, spreading across the upper Ohio Valley region through 00-03Z. The convective system roughly straddles a warm frontal zone, with rather stable air lingering across much of the upper Ohio Valley, to the northeast of the front. The southern flank of the convective system does extend southward into the warm sector, across parts of southern Ohio into northeastern Kentucky, and some northward advection of the front and boundary layer instability does seem possible across northwestern West Virginia and southeastern Ohio, toward the northern West Virginia Panhandle vicinity. This is expected to coincide with strengthening of southwesterly 850 mb flow in excess of 50 kt, which may contribute to an environment supportive of a continuing risk for potentially damaging wind gusts. An isolated tornado or two may be possible, but this threat may be mitigated by relatively dry air in lower levels.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm activity accompanied primarily by a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts will overspread the region through the 9-11 PM CDT time frame.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A broken pre-frontal line of thunderstorms is in the process of progressing east of the Mississippi River, where the boundary layer remains drier with dew points generally in the lower/mid 50s. With an upstream cold front continuing to surge through what is left of a plume of higher surface moisture content near/west of the Mississippi River, little further low-level moistening seems likely prior to the passage of the convective line (aside from from some surface dew point increases with the loss of daytime heating/mixing). It is possible, though, that present weak instability and forcing for ascent may be enough to maintain fairly vigorous convective development into the 02-04Z time. As long as storms maintain some strength, in the presence of 40-50 kt deep layer mean flow, a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts will probably continue.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging wind potential will continue across eastern portions of severe thunderstorm watch 28. Some threat may persist across east-central MS and trends will be monitored for potential downstream watch issuance later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A fast moving line of storms continues to track eastward from near the MS River into western MS. The 00z RAOB from JAN shows weak instability and a drier airmass with steep low and midlevel lapse rates. 0-6km shear is marginally supportive for supercells, and some weakly rotating embedded structures will continue to be possible. More likely, a damaging wind threat will continue eastward toward central MS this evening due to fast storm motion and steep low-level lapse rate environment. Some threat may ooze eastward outside of severe watch 28 into east-central MS and convective trends will be monitored for possible downstream watch issuance. ..Leitman.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will overspread the region through 11-2 AM EDT, accompanied by at least some risk for potentially damaging wind gusts. Another severe weather watch probably will be issued.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Some increase in low-level moisture (surface dew points perhaps rising from the lower through mid 50s) is possible on south/southwesterly low-level flow ahead of pre-frontal thunderstorm activity approaching the region. This should contribute to the maintenance of weak instability, despite the onset of diurnal boundary layer cooling. This may be enough to maintain the vigorous ongoing storms which appear likely to begin spreading east of tornado watch 31 and severe thunderstorm watch 32 during the 02-03Z time frame. In the presence of strong deep layer mean flow, including 50+ kt at 850 mb, storms will continue to pose a risk for at least localized damaging wind gusts until they weaken near the western slopes of the Appalachians later tonight. ..Kerr.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A large hail and strong wind risk will continue along and ahead of the cold front from portions of central into southeast TX and southwest LA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection has been struggling to intensify across portions of TX as the southward surging cold front quickly undercuts stronger updrafts. Some deeper, longer-lived convection has occurred near the Sabine Valley where golf ball size hail was reported around 02z in Vernon County, LA. The airmass ahead of the front continues to be weakly to moderately unstable with steep midlevel lapse rates in place per 00z LCH RAOB. Effective shear appears to be stronger across the eastern potion of the watch as well, which may further explain struggling convective trends further west. Regardless, any sustained convection along/ahead of the front will pose a large hail and perhaps strong wind threat for a few more hours this evening and severe thunderstorm watch 29 will continue. ..Leitman.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A risk for locally damaging wind gusts will continue with storms spreading into the western slopes of the central/southern Appalachians through 1-2 AM EDT. Additional watches to the east are not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The more intense leading edge of the pre-frontal thunderstorm development has been maintaining at least modest strength for the past hour or so. With some low-level moisture return evident within a residual axis of warmer boundary layer air ahead of it (where temperatures remain at or above 70f) into the western slopes of the central and southern Appalachians, activity may persist into the 05-06Z time frame before undergoing more notable weakening/ dissipation. Until this occurs, it will continue to pose a risk for localized damaging surface gusts. ..Kerr.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Localized damaging wind gusts may remain possible with the remnant line of convection spreading toward the Interstate 85 corridor through 1-4 AM EDT. Additional watches to the east are not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Lightning and radar data indicate notable weakening trends to convection extending south of the southern Tennessee state border during the past hour or so. However, latest surface and objective analysis suggests that the boundary layer remains at least weakly unstable ahead of activity into the Interstate 85 corridor of east central Alabama and northwest Georgia. With activity still embedded within 30-50 kt lower/mid tropospheric mean flow, it probably will continue to pose a risk for localized strong surface gusts until it dissipates later tonight. ..Kerr.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Remaining valid portion of WWs 29 and 33 may be allowed to expire as scheduled at Midnight CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Conglomerate convective outflow continues to gradually advance southward into the vicinity of the Gulf coast. Remnant stronger convection has become widely scattered, and generally confined to boundary intersections. Although an inflow of weak to moderately unstable air may still be supporting this activity, low-level wind fields are in the process of weakening below 20-30 kt. While isolated strong storm development may linger across western into central Gulf coastal areas through 06-09Z, further severe weather potential appears negligible enough that additional watches are not anticipated. ..Kerr.. 04/04/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat for wind damage and hail will likely continue for a few more hours with the stronger parts of a line moving through the southern and central Appalachians. Additional WW issuance will likely not be needed. Any lingering severe threat can be handled by a local extension.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar imagery shows a squall line from eastern Kentucky extending south-southwestward across eastern Tennessee into far northwest Georgia and central Alabama. The strongest instability is located ahead of the southern part of the line where MLCAPE values are between 500 and 1000 J/kg as evidenced by the 05Z Birmingham sounding. For this reason, the line may retain a marginal wind-damage threat for a few more hours as it moves eastward across eastern Alabama, northwestern Georgia and eastern Tennessee. Locations just to the east of the watch may need to a local extension in area and time issued. On the northern part of the line, instability is very weak across western Virginia. Although a marginal wind-damage threat could linger, this part of the line should weaken quickly as it moves into the higher terrain of the central Appalachians.
